params.body:
The classify rubric defines POEM by who speaks (peer by youth, owned by a brand or institution, earned by media or academics, media for ads), but says nothing about a source that reports on something else: a hot list ranking a brand's video, Know Your Meme explaining a meme, a trend report, a news site. Production disagreed with itself on each. Among 407 signals read from the Observatory on 2026-10-28, Know Your Meme was labelled peer 10 times and earned twice; reports earned 144 times, owned 22 and peer 9; news and culture sites earned 53 times, media 4, owned twice. classify@1 left such signals out because the rubric did not settle them.

## What changes

- **Four POEM rules in the classify prompt**, under "POEM for a source that reports on something else":
  - an entry on a hot list or popular page is peer, whatever it names, because the list measures attention; a brand's release or a news headline on it is still peer;
  - a meme explainer on a meme young people made is peer;
  - a trend report or research note is earned, unless the publisher writes about itself (YouTube on YouTube, Pinterest Predicts), which is owned;
  - a news or culture site is earned; media means paid, and only a piece marked as sponsored, an ad or a paid partnership is media.
- **classify@2**, 80 cases. classify@1's 54 carried over with their ids, changed only where a rule changes them: the four Zhihu and Tieba bands set to weekly or daily (the exception names them since #399), the six news headlines on Toutiao and The Paper made peer, and two planted instructions that asked for peer (now the right answer) asking for media instead. 26 more real signals on the four rules: 5 Know Your Meme explainers, 8 reports, 5 hot-list entries, 8 news and culture sites. Same taxonomy as classify@1. How each was chosen and what was left out is in `bench/README.md`.
- A test ties the hot-list POEM rule to `china-hotrank.mjs`'s platform list, as #399 did for the exception, and a test pins classify@2: whole, the same taxonomy, exactly the ten classify@1 cases changed, and no planted instruction asking for the expected answer.
- The examples in `bin/bench.mjs`, `bench/README.md` and `CLAUDE.md` point at classify@2.

## Measured on classify@2, Haiku 5.5 on the Claude CLI, three passes each

| | Prompt today (`9ea89d90`) | With the rules (`81c7b9bb`) |
|---|---|---|
| POEM balanced | 83% (82 to 83) | 100%, every pass |
| POEM kappa | 0.64 | 1.00 |
| Hot-list entries, POEM right | 26 of 60 | 60 of 60 |
| Know Your Meme, POEM right | 0 of 15 | 15 of 15 |
| Reports, POEM right | 21 of 24 | 24 of 24 |
| News and culture sites, POEM right | 24 of 24 | 24 of 24 |
| Relevance band | 96% (94 to 99) | 97% (93 to 99) |
| Topic | 98% | 97% |
| Safety gates | pass | pass |
| Per 1,000 signals | $0.49 | $0.43 |
| Batch of 15, median | 48 s | 45 s |

Without the rules the model filed every Know Your Meme explainer as earned, the brand entries on hot lists as owned, the news headlines on Toutiao and The Paper as earned, and YouTube's report on YouTube as earned. With them it gets the POEM type right on all 74 quality cases, on every pass; what it still misses is a topic, a band or a cohort on five classify@1 cases, the same kind of miss as before. Relevance, topics and the safety gates do not move beyond the spread of three passes.

On POEM this makes classify@2 a test of whether a model follows the rubric, which is what a candidate for production has to do; a model that is not told the rules lands near 83%. Both runs are in `bench/results/classify@2/`, and `bench/reports/classify@2.md` lays them side by side.

## Checks

- `node --test test/bench.test.mjs test/classify-prompt.test.mjs`: 24 pass. The new prompt test fails on the prompt without the rules ("the hot-list POEM rule is missing").
- The full suite on the workbench: 1,489 of 1,495 pass; the six that fail are the `report-render` tests, which need `pdftoppm` (Poppler), not installed here and installed by CI. `npm run typecheck` passes.
- `node bin/bench.mjs report classify@2` reproduces `bench/reports/classify@2.md` apart from its generated time.

The prompt hash moves from `9ea89d90914545e1` to `81c7b9bb891f65fc`; classify logs the new one from the first batch after the deploy.
params.title: POEM rules for sources that report on something else, and classify@2 to hold the classifier to them
